recommendation_summary: The reply's recommendation for now is to keep the shared folder for drafts and add a protected release archive. The archive would store each exact approved document, record the reviewer's authenticated identity and approval time, block self-approval, and lock the document and its evidence for seven years. It explicitly rejects the APPROVED column as meeting the contract and offers no optional additions. Still open: the agent asks which system hosts the folder, because that decides whether these controls fit the existing setup.

labels.Requirements and who asked: The signed customer contract requires exact approved versions, approver identity and approval time retained for seven years, independent approval, and protection from later edits; you prefer keeping the folder.
labels.Deleted: Typed initials and naming conventions as approval controls.
labels.Bottleneck: Authors can edit the folder, so it cannot reliably preserve the approved release and its approval evidence.
labels.Checked myself: Only the facts you provided; the folder system’s capabilities remain unverified.

note: All four labelled lines come before the recommendation, and the chosen archive ties a non-author's authenticated approval and time to the exact document version and locks both for the retention period.
